title: House Robber II
statement: Same rule as House Robber — never rob two adjacent houses — but now the houses stand in a **circle**, so the first and the last house are neighbours too. Return the maximum amount you can rob.

example.why: On a straight street 2 + 9 + 1 = 12 would work, but in a circle house 0 and house 4 are neighbours. The best is 2 + 9 = 11.

idea: The only new rule: the first and the last house cannot **both** be robbed.
So one of them is certainly left alone. Case A: house 0 is left out → an ordinary straight street of houses `1 … n − 1`. Case B: the last house is left out → a straight street of houses `0 … n − 2`.
Solve both with the ordinary House Robber (here with two variables instead of an array) and return the larger result.

complexity.spaceWhy: The two slices; the robbing itself uses only two variables.

steps.text: Our example: **`nums = [2,7,9,3,1]`**. Each step runs one highlighted line of the code.
